subject.title: [Feature] Allow configuring Gemini safety settings in OpenClaw

question: Should OpenClaw expose a first-class Gemini safety-settings config knob, and if so what exact schema, category set, thresholds, request precedence, and Google-only scope should it support?
rationale: This changes provider request behavior and can relax upstream safety filtering, so automation should not choose the public config contract or safety posture without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow Google setting
options.body: Add a strict Google-scoped models.providers.*.safetySettings or equivalent contract with documented categories, thresholds, request precedence, and focused tests.

options.title: Keep provider defaults only
options.body: Decline the config surface for now and keep Gemini safety behavior on upstream provider defaults to avoid adding a safety-affecting knob.

options.title: Design a broader provider-settings seam
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define a general provider-specific request-settings API that can cover Google and future provider-owned controls.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow Google setting
recommendation.body: Add a strict Google-scoped models.providers.*.safetySettings or equivalent contract with documented categories, thresholds, request precedence, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest current routing signal from the discussion plus recent history on the affected Google transport/config files.
